source.title: Takeuchi's Information Criteria as Generalization Measures for DNNs Close to NTK Regime
source.authors: Hiroki Naganuma; Taiji Suzuki; Rio Yokota; M. Nomura; Kohta Ishikawa; Ikuro Sato

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether TIC estimates track the training–test generalization gap across model and dataset settings. This is a conceptual test of a measured property related to the claim, but it does not test any listed version's specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations between TIC estimates and the generalization gap. It does not test memorization of random labels, interpolation-threshold behavior, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Cited results about other measures are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates TIC estimates against loss-based generalization gaps, a different measure from V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness. Its raw Hessian-trace comparisons also do not measure V7. Widening changes TIC–gap correlation, without testing V2's test-error trend beyond interpolation. No own result tests V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: approximate TIC tracks generalization gaps in settings they consider close to the NTK regime, loses correlation outside that regime, tracks gaps during training, and improves trial pruning in one CIFAR-10/ResNet-8 experiment. Their NTK interpretation relies on proxies rather than direct kernel-stability diagnostics.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures TIC, based on the Hessian and gradient covariance, rather than the interventions or measures in the listed versions. Training used Bayesian hyperparameter optimization; batch normalization and data augmentation were omitted.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlation varied by architecture, dataset, skip connections, and d/n setting. The authors report weaker or inverse correlations in some TinyMNIST settings and stronger correlations in several larger d/n settings. Batch normalization and data augmentation were not used.

fits_no_version.finding: TIC lower-bound estimates have architecture- and dataset-dependent correlations with absolute training–test loss gaps: Pearson coefficients range from -0.766 to 0.983 in Table 7. Reducing the dataset or widening a network increases correlation in Table 13.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TIC estimates can track loss-based generalization gaps in some workloads, with effectiveness depending on architecture, approximation, and parameter-to-sample ratio.

record.problems: The paper states that the experimental configurations omit batch normalization and data augmentation. The correlation values are reported without uncertainty estimates. The authors note that d/n alone is not sufficient to establish NTK proximity and leave more refined NTK diagnostics for future work. The HPO demonstration is limited to one setting.
record.rows_left_out: Table 7 separately reports Spearman and Kendall correlations for the same 15 model–dataset settings; these metric-specific rows were omitted to prioritize the main Pearson results and keep the extraction compact. Table 13 also reports Spearman and Kendall correlations for four settings, omitted for the same reason. Tables 8–10 report correlations for alternative TIC approximations on TinyMNIST, and other figures report training-process and practical-scale approximation comparisons; these were omitted to prioritize the main across-workload correlation results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test-error changes with width beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out error and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across dataset sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples compared with equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All reported Pearson values match the supplied tables. Negative TIC correlations are not reversals of any listed version. Raw Hessian-trace failures in Figures 14 and 16 do not challenge magnitude-aware sharpness. The study proposes systematic comparison with sharpness measures as future work.

versions.untested_parts: Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and local connectivity.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
